title: Worth it for the cherry blossom and rose stamps
text:
Worth it for the cherry blossom and rose stamps. I managed to land the [[ASIN:B00ABH0PYI OXO Good Grips Cookie Press with Disk Storage Case]] as a Vine item, and fell madly in love with it. I have an older Swedish metal cookie press that is built like a tank, but the trigger mechanism was hard on my arthritis. The OXO press, on the other hand, is as simple as loading the press with dough (the included booklet contains three base recipes for cream cheese, butter, and and chocolate shortbread spritz dough with several variations) and pressing down on the handle. I'd tried about six of the twelve included disks, but wanted something for spring (St. Pat's, Valentine's, etc.)

Enter the Springtime Disk Set, with gives you an additional six disks for your OXO cookie press: a cherry blossom, rose, LOVE stamp, two hearts, a shamrock, and a bouquet of flowers.

For St. Pat's, I made a double batch of green-tinted shamrocks with green sprinkles.

I'd specifically purchased this set for the cherry blossom stamp; as I have many Japan Air Self-Defense Force wingmen that I work with, I wanted to make up sakura (cherry blossom) cookie bags during hanami (cherry blossom viewing season). I ended up making a split batch of colored-and-sprinkled cherry blossoms and roses and packaging them in cellophane bags, and they were a hit! (see photo above) I used the OXO standard butter dough recipe that came with my press, although I've also tried the chocolate shortbread and lemon poppyseed variations, and they were also good (you can also find the recipes on the OXO website; see comments for the link).

One addition that would have been nice would have been an additional plastic storage case for the disks; the original storage case that came with [[ASIN:B00ABH0PYI OXO Good Grips Cookie Press with Disk Storage Case]] has slots for exactly 12 disks to keep them upright, and then I had to throw in the additional six disks from the Springtime set with no way to keep them from banging into the disks next to them.
